newsitem.title: USA: Slower cash trade presses nearby CME lumber.
newsitem.headline: Slower cash trade presses nearby CME lumber.

text.p: Long liquidation on reports that cash trade has slowed pressured nearby CME lumber futures while thinly traded distant months ranged mixed, traders said.
Lumber closed $4.90 per tbf lower to $5.50 higher with July off most at $387.50 and September off $0.20 at $380.80 per tbf.

July was under pressure from the start as reports of slowing cash trade offset strong demand last week when cash prices moved sharply higher. Other liquidation was also developing in July ahead of its spot position next week, traders said.
Carryover fund demand supported September early following Friday's limit gain. But that month also ran into resistance, both from technicals and the concern over slowing cash trade, they added.
